trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information of at least 500 consumers without authorization; unauthorized access is presumed to be acquisition unless reliable evidence shows otherwise (314.2(m))
deadline: As soon as possible, and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC, electronically on the ftc.gov form. Content: firm name and contact; types of information; date or date range; number of consumers; general description; any written law enforcement determination and contact (314.4(j)(1)(i)-(vi))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more consumers (individual tax clients); business entities are not counted
clock_starts: Discovery: first day the event is known to any employee, officer, or other agent other than the attacker (314.4(j)(2))

trigger: A law enforcement official gives a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Official may request an initial delay of up to 30 days after the FTC notice, extendable by up to 60 days on written request
notify: Include the determination and the official's contact in the FTC notice
applies_at_this_tier: If requested. It delays public disclosure by the FTC, not the firm's filing

citation: IRS Pub. 1345 (Rev. 12-2025), Reporting of Security Incidents (N54-R03)
trigger: Any event that can result in unauthorized disclosure, misuse, modification, or destruction of taxpayer information
deadline: As soon as possible but not later than the next business day after confirmation of the incident
notify: IRS. EROs contact their local Stakeholder Liaison following the Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals instructions
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Authorized IRS e-file Provider (ERO) with 30 EFINs; one report covers all affected EFINs, including AF-05 and AF-06

citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance, not a regulation) (N54-R03)
trigger: Client data stolen or accessed by an unauthorized person
deadline: As quickly as possible ('Speed is critical'); in practice the same call as the Pub. 1345 report
notify: Local IRS Stakeholder Liaison, who notifies IRS Criminal Investigation and others in the IRS
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance)
trigger: Data theft affecting clients for whom the firm prepares state returns
deadline: As quickly as possible, alongside the IRS report
notify: Each state tax agency where affected clients file, using the Federation of Tax Administrators contact list
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Florida has no personal income tax; notify the agencies of the other states where affected clients file

citation: IRS Data Theft Information for Tax Professionals (guidance); OFAC advisory (2021-09-21) on reporting
trigger: Data theft; attempted or completed refund diversion; extortion
deadline: As soon as possible after declaration
notify: FBI field office or IC3; Secret Service if directed
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Also needed for any no-harm consultation under state law

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
trigger: Breach of personal information as each state defines it (definitions, triggers, and harm thresholds vary)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents, by the methods and with the content each state requires
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Clients in all 50 states; counsel applies the updated state matrix (POAM-023)
clock_starts: Each state's trigger (often determination or discovery of the breach)

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above the state's threshold (some states require notice for any breach of residents)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorneys general or other designated agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, where thresholds are met

trigger: Notice to more than the state-set number of residents
deadline: Varies by state (often without unreasonable delay)
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, where thresholds are met

trigger: Breach of security: unauthorized access of electronic personal information (for example, name with SSN; name with a financial account number and required access code; an email address or user name with a password)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email. Content: date or date range, description of the information, and firm contact information
applies_at_this_tier: Yes
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to the notice to individuals)
notify: Department of Legal Affairs. Content: synopsis, number of Floridians, free services offered, copy of the individual notice, firm contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies: timing, distribution, and content of the notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000
clock_starts: When the individual notices are set

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the firm reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely for this incident type: stolen tax documents are used for refund fraud. Counsel decides

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: If requested

trigger: Notice given under the rules of the firm's primary or functional federal regulator
deadline: Deemed compliant only if the firm notifies individuals under those rules and timely gives the Department a copy
notify: n/a
applies_at_this_tier: No for this incident. The FTC Safeguards Rule requires notice to the FTC only, not to individuals, so Florida individual and Department notices must be sent. Counsel confirms

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the firm (inbound, worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system a vendor maintains for the firm (for example, the DMS, transmitter, or AI provider)
deadline: Agent notifies the firm as expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination
notify: The firm, which then gives the (3) and (4) notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Contract terms tracked in the notice register (POAM-023)

obligation: Firm as third-party agent to SL-1 and SL-2 clients (outbound, worked example)
trigger: Breach of personal information the firm maintains or processes on behalf of a client business (for example, SL-1 payroll data for client employees)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination; contracts may be shorter
notify: Each affected client business, with all information it needs to give its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for SL-1 and SL-2 data; worked example of each state's agent duty

obligation: Business associate breach notice to covered entity clients (outbound)
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held for a health care client
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery; business associate agreements are often shorter
notify: Each affected covered entity client, with the identity of each individual and the information it needs for its own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if PHI was involved (audit workpapers, consulting data rooms)
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any employee, officer, or agent (164.410(a)(2))

obligation: Subcontractor breach notice to the firm (inbound)
citation: 45 CFR 164.410 (applies to subcontractors as business associates)
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI at a subcontractor
deadline: No later than 60 calendar days after the subcontractor's discovery, or sooner per the agreement
notify: The firm, which then notifies its covered entity clients
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

citation: Client contracts (24 to 72 hours); SEC Release 33-11216 (registrants are not exempt from Item 1.05 disclosure for incidents on third-party systems they use)
trigger: Incident affecting an SEC-registrant client's data or services (issuer audit data, SL-1 or SL-2 data, tax provision work)
deadline: Within each contract's term; the Incident Disclosure Committee aims for 48 hours after confirmation
notify: Client's designated security or legal contact, so the client can make its own materiality determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. This is the firm's contractual duty; the 8-K duty is the client's

obligation: Other client contract notices (SL-1, SL-2, advisory)
trigger: Incident affecting client data or services
deadline: Per contract (tracked in the notice register, POAM-023)
notify: Client contacts named in agreements
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC
applies_at_this_tier: No. The firm is a private partnership, not an SEC registrant (Fla. Stat. 473.309(1)(b) requires CPA ownership)

citation: FAR 52.204-21 (N54-R04) has no incident reporting paragraph; individual contracts may add agency terms
trigger: Incident affecting Federal Contract Information
deadline: Per contract terms
notify: Contracting officer named in the contract
applies_at_this_tier: Check each of the about 30 contracts; FAR cyber incident reporting rule is proposed only

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Only if identified; the firm holds federal contracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services) in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Only if identified; the firm holds federal contracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article subject to a FASCSA order in use or delivered
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days)
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the clause is in a contract and an article is identified

trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
notify: DoD via https://dibnet.dod.mil
applies_at_this_tier: No. The firm has no DoD contracts

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: An extortion demand is considered for payment (data theft extortion is possible after a business email compromise)
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand arises (POL-03 4.8)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then)

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier breach hotline before hiring vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Contractual, not legal

trigger: Incident that could lead to client claims
deadline: Per policy
notify: Professional liability carrier
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. Contractual
